verdict.rationale: Pipecat has no built-in natural-language control surface. It does support operation through a coding agent: `pipecat context-hub install` registers a local MCP server with the user's coding agent, the quickstart scaffold writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, and an llms.txt is served. The probe confirms the context-hub command exists in the official CLI. Natural-language operation therefore depends on an external agent (a substantial limitation) rather than being a native capability. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language command interface for driving the CLI or Cloud, documented end-to-end examples of operating Pipecat via natural language, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven workflows.
